scenario.name: CNCF Kubernetes Security, Microsoft Defender for Cloud & MITRE T1609 — Kubelet Read/Write Port 10250 & etcd Snapshot Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine an apartment tower whose floor-manager desk has no receptionist, no sign-in book, and an open intercom linking every suite. Any unbadged visitor can walk up to the desk to grab the complete tenant directory, speak an order straight into the maintenance penthouse to unlock the boiler room, and photograph the entire building master safe archive stored on the control floor. In this scenario (T1613, CNCF Kubernetes Security, Microsoft Defender for Cloud & MITRE T1609, Kubelet Read/Write Port 10250 & etcd Snapshot Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: unauthenticated Pod Enumeration via Kubelet, then remote Command Execution Inside Privileged, then control-Plane etcd Snapshot Extraction. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Unauthenticated Pod Enumeration via Kubelet, then Remote Command Execution Inside Privileged, then Control-Plane etcd Snapshot Extraction. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1613 across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Unauthenticated Pod Enumeration via Kubelet /pods Endpoint (:10250)
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1613 - Container and Resource Discovery)
stages.description: Walking up to the unguarded floor-manager desk, the intruder asks for the full occupancy clipboard without showing a single badge. The desk gladly hands back every suite number, resident name, and which suites hold master maintenance keys. When Kubelet runs with --anonymous-auth=true and --authorization-mode=AlwaysAllow, any pod or host on the node network can query https://<node_ip>:10250/pods to retrieve full PodSpecs, environment variables, and mounted volume paths running on that worker node (logged in Linux Audit Event 10250 with KubeletEndpoint=GET /pods , :10250, AuthenticatedUser=system:anonymous, AuthorizationMode=AlwaysAllow , Misconfigured so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes curl -sk https://10.10.20.11:10250/pods | jq ".items[].metadata.name" (which executes the HTTP/HTTPS transfer client , curl -sk https://10.10.20.11:10250/pods | jq ".items[].metadata.name" to transmit crafted exploit request so that delivers the network exploit payload or retrieves the next-stage execution script , T1613 during "Unauthenticated Pod Enumeration via Kubelet /pods Endpoint , :10250" over HTTP/HTTPS). Next, the follow-up artifact ps aux | grep kubelet | grep -- "--anonymous-auth" runs (which executes or inspects a container runtime or Kubernetes control-plane operation , ps aux | grep kubelet | grep -- "--anonymous-auth" involving OCI c so that provides forensic visibility and runtime verification for container boundary isolation or cluster secret access , T1613 during "Unauthenticated Pod Enumeration via Kubelet /pods Endpoint , :10250"). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ GET /pods HTTP/1.1 (Kubelet API Port 10250 Anonymous Request) / ⇠#1 ACK 10250) from Node ① (#1 Internal Pod / Node Scanner) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 etcd Key-Value Store (:2379)).

keySpecs.value: Set --anonymous-auth=false and --authorization-mode=Webhook in /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml across all worker nodes and block port 10250 from pod CIDR ranges.

stages.title: Stage 2: Remote Command Execution Inside Privileged Pod via Kubelet /run Endpoint
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1609 - Container Administration Command)
stages.description: Picking the most privileged maintenance suite straight off the occupancy clipboard, the intruder presses the desk direct intercom button and issues live work orders inside that suite as though standing inside the room personally. Using the pod namespace, pod name, and container name discovered from /pods, a POST request to /run/<namespace>/<pod>/<container> instructs Kubelet to invoke the CRI ExecSync RPC on containerd, executing arbitrary commands inside a privileged kube-system pod (logged in Linux Audit Event 59 with KubeletApiAction=POST /run/kube-system/kube-proxy-x892a/kube-proxy, TargetNamespace=kube-system, CriOperation=ExecSync via containerd-shim-runc-v2 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes curl -sk -X POST "https://10.10.20.11:10250/run/kube-system/kube-proxy-x892a/kube-proxy" -d "cmd=cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token" (which executes the HTTP/HTTPS transfer client , curl -sk -X POST "https://10.10.20.11:10250/run/kube-system/kube-proxy-x892a/kube-proxy" -d "cmd=cat /var so that delivers the network exploit payload or retrieves the next-stage execution script , T1609 during "Remote Command Execution Inside Privileged Pod via Kubelet /run Endpoint" over HTTP/HTTPS). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ POST /run/kube-system/kube-proxy-x892a/kube-proxy cmd=cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token / ⇠#2 ACK 59) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Kubelet HTTPS API (:10250)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 etcd Key-Value Store (:2379)).

keySpecs.value: Monitor kubelet journald logs and CRI containerd events for /run or /exec requests that do not originate from the control-plane kube-apiserver IP.

stages.title: Stage 3: Control-Plane etcd Snapshot Extraction (/var/lib/etcd/member/snap/db)
stages.subtitle: Credential Access (T1552.007 - Unsecured Credentials: Container API)
stages.description: Standing inside a control-floor suite with direct access to the vault certificates, the intruder takes a complete instant photograph of the building master ledger cabinet, capturing every resident key, rulebook, and secret stored across the entire tower. If the compromised node hosts control-plane static pods or mounts /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd, etcdctl snapshot save dumps the entire cluster state database (/registry/secrets/*), which DFIR analysts verify in etcd gRPC access logs and auditd file reads (logged in Linux Audit Event 2379 with DatabaseTarget=etcd , :2379 /var/lib/etcd/member/snap/db, OutputArtifact=/tmp/etcd-snapshot.db, KeyPrefixTargeted=/registry/secrets/kube-system/ so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snapshot.db (which executes or inspects a container runtime or Kubernetes control-plane operation , ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert= so that provides forensic visibility and runtime verification for container boundary isolation or cluster secret access , T1552.007 during "Control-Plane etcd Snapshot Extraction , /var/lib/etcd/member/snap/db"). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snapshot.db / ⇠#3 ACK 2379) from Node ③ (#3 Kubelet HTTPS API (:10250)) to Node ④ (#4 Container Runtime (containerd)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 etcd Key-Value Store (:2379)).

keySpecs.value: Enable Kubernetes EncryptionConfiguration (AES-CBC or KMS v2) at rest for Secrets stored in etcd so offline snapshots of /var/lib/etcd/member/snap/db do not expose plaintext credentials.
